His historical record includes chronicles of peoples who have achieved it and lost it, among them the Greeks, the Romans, the Persians, the Israelites, the Arabs, and the Blacks of Abyssinia. This capacity, however, requires the necessary environmental and climatic conditions to fully manifest.
zh: 这显然不是伊本·赫勒敦的视角。他没有把任何一个人群作为衡量人性的标准。他的中世纪世界观更多以宗教而非族群为中心。然而，尽管伊本·赫勒敦生活在穆斯林社会，并且作为信徒和臣民似乎都认同其意识形态，他的著作却构成一种理性主义探究，明显独立于、区别于其时代的神学框架。

《历史绪论》探讨王朝权力如何获得、丧失并在人群之间转移，表明只要气候与社会条件适宜，任何群体内部都能产生umrân，它绝非任何单一群体的专属，而是不断易手。伊本·赫勒敦承认伊斯兰作为信仰的优越性，却认为umrân——即科学、技艺以及与王朝行政相联系的等级的创生——是人类能力与理性的产物。他的历史记录包括取得又失去这种成就的各人群编年史，其中有希腊人、罗马人、波斯人、以色列人、阿拉伯人，以及阿比西尼亚的黑人。不过，这种能力需要必要的环境与气候条件，才能充分显现。

en: It is in translation that Ibn Khaldûn’s thought is often reconfigured. Colonial translators and interpreters imposed racial categories foreign to both him and his time, producing a text that appears highly racialized, prejudicial, and offensive to modern sensibilities. In the Arabic original, these categories are instead climatic and environmental, describing the limits and possibilities for human societies without invoking fixed hierarchies of race. Reading Ibn Khaldûn within his historical and linguistic context reveals a thinker who analyzed human diversity in terms of social, environmental, and political conditions rather than biological determinism.
zh: 伊本·赫勒敦的思想往往正是在翻译中被重新配置。殖民译者和阐释者强加了与他本人及其时代均不相容的种族范畴，生产出一个在现代人的感受中显得高度种族化、充满偏见且具有冒犯性的文本。在阿拉伯语原文中，这些范畴却是气候性与环境性的，用来描述人类社会的限制和可能性，而不诉诸固定的种族等级。在历史和语言语境中阅读伊本·赫勒敦，会显露出这样一位思想家：他以社会、环境和政治条件，而非生物决定论，来分析人类多样性。

en: In these translations, Ibn Khaldûn’s language, categories, and even his judgments are reformulated into the language and categories of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Unpacking the translations and confronting them, using a philological method, alongside the Arabic text reveals that the original work bears no resemblance to the racial texts or racial thinking of the translations.
zh: 在这些译本中，伊本·赫勒敦的语言、范畴，甚至判断，都被重新表述为18和19世纪的语言与范畴。用语文学方法剖析译本，并将其与阿拉伯语文本对照，就会发现原作与译本中的种族文本或种族思维并不相似。

en: His categories are climatic and environmental. This does not mean that they are unproblematic, neutral, or free of bias. It means, rather, that they belong to a different epistemic register, one that carries its own hierarchies but not the hierarchy of race. Nor are they embedded in forms of power organized around race in the modern sense or structured for purposes of conquest and rule. By contrast, the categories introduced through translation are fully consistent with a racial framework, one that emerged in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries and that served to organize difference within projects of imperial domination. Reading him within his context, against the colonial archive, reveals a thinker who explained human diversity (as it pertains to

as a social formation) in terms of environment, social organization, and historical circumstance, rather than fixed racial hierarchies. Comparing the translations with the original text thus recovers Ibn Khaldûn’s medieval epistemic framework and restores the analytical categories that colonial translators replaced with their own.
zh: 他的范畴是气候性与环境性的。这并不意味着它们没有问题、保持中立或毫无偏见，而是说，它们属于另一种知识层次，自有其等级，却不是种族等级。它们也不嵌入现代意义上围绕种族组织起来、或以征服和统治为目的构造起来的权力形式。相比之下，通过翻译引入的范畴完全符合一种种族框架；这一框架兴起于18和19世纪，服务于帝国支配计划中对差异的组织。将他置于自身语境中，并对照殖民档案来阅读，会显露出一位以环境、社会组织和历史条件，而非固定种族等级，解释人类多样性的思想家；这里的多样性，是就ʿumrân作为社会形态而言的。因此，将译本与原文比较，可以重新找回伊本·赫勒敦的中世纪知识框架，恢复被殖民译者以自身范畴取代的分析范畴。

en: Conclusion
zh: 结论

en: Ibn Khaldûn as a problem, at its core, is a problem of how non-Western knowledge and its figures are appropriated through acts of translation that remake them into Western knowledge regulated by a Western episteme. This becomes a challenge in the sociology of knowledge, since research in this area often confronts a corpus whose author is ostensibly non-Western while its discourse has been remade within Western frameworks. Hence my argument in this article: that there is Ibn Khaldûn, the medieval author, and there is Ibn Khaldûn, the colonial author—the latter emerging within the colonial context as a product of the French translation that subsequently influenced the English one.
zh: 伊本·赫勒敦这一问题，其核心在于：非西方知识及其代表人物如何通过翻译行为被挪用，并被重塑为受西方知识型规制的西方知识。这成为知识社会学中的一项挑战，因为这一领域的研究常常面对这样一批文本：其作者表面上是非西方的，其话语却已在西方框架中被重新制作。由此便有了本文的论点：存在一位中世纪作者伊本·赫勒敦，也存在一位殖民作者伊本·赫勒敦；后者出现在殖民语境中，是法译本的产物，而法译本随后又影响了英译本。

en: Ibn Khaldûn has largely circulated as a colonial author whose French and English texts are fraught with colonial categories, producing a discursivity on the Maghreb, Muslim historiography, and Muslim self-representation. In translation, Ibn Khaldûn appears as racist, especially in statements about what the translations call Negroes or

To read or hear his name is to think simultaneously of intellectual brilliance and of perceptions of cultural backwardness—the former often highlighting the latter. His name has come to overshadow much of the historiographic tradition of his time and afterward, shaping how later scholars engage with medieval Arab historiography. Some of this tradition developed directly from his work, while much of the rest emerged independently. Yet Ibn Khaldûn’s name “shines” against the context in which he emerged, perceived by later Orientalists as a light in what was thought to be darkness, much as a flame appears brightest at night.
zh: 伊本·赫勒敦主要以殖民作者的形态流传，其法文与英文文本充满殖民范畴，生产出关于马格里布、穆斯林史学和穆斯林自我表述的话语性。在翻译中，伊本·赫勒敦显得具有种族主义，尤其是在谈论译本所称的Negroes或Nègres时。读到或听到他的名字，便会同时想到思想上的卓越与文化落后的印象，前者往往凸显后者。他的名字逐渐遮蔽了其时代及后世的大部分史学传统，塑造了后来学者研究中世纪阿拉伯史学的方式。这一传统有一部分直接从其著作发展而来，另有很大一部分则独立产生。然而，伊本·赫勒敦的名字在其产生的背景映衬下“闪耀”；后来的东方学家将他视为所谓黑暗中的一道光，正如火焰在夜晚显得最明亮。

en: Ibn Khaldûn in translation cannot be dismissed as merely “erroneous” or “distorted.” The colonial author exists in his own right. By himself, he constitutes a real colonial archive: a repository of racial judgments, ideological assumptions, and conceptual distortions. He has thrived and will continue to do so unless the act of translation itself is critically examined—unless we ask how these translations were shaped by racial ideology, power, and epistemic assumptions. Translation ideology is central to any translation, but especially in colonial contexts, where language, power, and race intersect.
Even today, AI translation, often informed by existing Orientalist categories, risks reproducing these frameworks as seemingly objective knowledge.
zh: 不能把翻译中的伊本·赫勒敦仅仅视为“错误”或“扭曲”而加以否定。这位殖民作者具有自身的存在。他自己便构成一份真实的殖民档案：一个储存种族判断、意识形态预设与概念扭曲的库藏。他已蓬勃发展，并将继续如此，除非翻译行为本身受到批判性审视——除非我们追问，这些译本如何受到种族意识形态、权力和知识预设的塑造。翻译意识形态对任何翻译都至关重要，在语言、权力与种族相互交织的殖民语境中尤其如此。
即使在今天，人工智能翻译也常常受到既有东方学范畴的影响，因而有把这些框架再生产为貌似客观知识的风险。

en: Rather than disregarding the colonial Ibn Khaldûn, we ought to decolonize him—not only his work in translation but also the ensemble of ideas, judgments, and assumptions about him that extend beyond his original texts. Such an approach allows us to consider the history of how colonial powers turned the local into the colonial, produced knowledge about the Other, and instrumentalized this knowledge to create identities and histories, opening colonial horizons even in a postcolonial world. Formerly colonized peoples, despite later claims of independence, were caught in webs of colonial significance they did not themselves weave.
zh: 我们不应无视殖民伊本·赫勒敦，而应使其去殖民化：不仅处理翻译中的著作，也处理超出其原始文本、围绕他形成的整套观念、判断与预设。这种路径使我们能够考察殖民权力如何将地方性的事物转化为殖民性的事物，如何生产关于他者的知识，并将这些知识工具化，以创造身份与历史，即使在后殖民世界中也开启殖民视域。曾被殖民的人民，尽管后来宣称独立，却仍被困在并非由自己编织的殖民意义之网中。

en: Because translation is an epistemic field—not only a locus of colonial otherness—decolonizing Ibn Khaldûn also means decolonizing European knowledge itself. It is an intellectual endeavor to rewrite the history of knowledge production in the colonies and, in doing so, to rethink European history and sociology within the larger context of colonial rule and difference. This perspective highlights that, during the formative years of social science, knowledge production was already at work through epistemic encounters. European sociology and history emerged not only from the metropole but also from the colonies themselves, at the linguistic and epistemic intersection with the then-colonial center.
zh: 由于翻译是一个知识领域，而不仅是殖民他者性的场所，使伊本·赫勒敦去殖民化，也意味着使欧洲知识本身去殖民化。这是一项思想工作，旨在重写殖民地知识生产的历史，并借此在殖民统治与差异的更大背景中重新思考欧洲历史和社会学。这一视角强调，在社会科学形成之初，知识生产就已通过不同知识之间的相遇而展开。欧洲社会学和历史学不仅来自宗主国，也来自殖民地本身，产生于殖民地与当时殖民中心的语言及知识交汇处。

en: Considering the intense focus on Ibn Khaldûn—the man, the statesman, and the author—decolonizing him also provides an example of how non-Western thinkers are co-opted and celebrated paradoxically: individual brilliance is recognized while the contributions of their cultural milieu are minimized, marginalized, or erased. This erasure is evident in his absence from the history of European and American sociology, despite the influence of his concepts on Durkheim and Bourdieu. Such absences contribute to the enduring perception of sociology as a predominantly European discipline, untouched by social thought from other traditions. Even when historians investigate the colonial origins of the social sciences, the intellectual traditions encountered, used, or appropriated by Europeans are often silenced. Decolonizing Ibn Khaldûn, therefore, means recovering an intellectual heritage that shaped European thought and opening the way to a plural history of sociology—not to diminish Durkheim, Bourdieu, or any other sociologist or anthropologist whose ideas resonate with Ibn Khaldûn, but to show how colonialism created a global field in which ideas circulated, unevenly structured by colonial power.
zh: 考虑到人们对伊本·赫勒敦这位个人、政治家和作者的高度关注，使他去殖民化，也提供了一个例子，展示非西方思想家如何被吸纳并以矛盾方式受到赞颂：个人的才华得到承认，其文化环境的贡献却被缩小、边缘化或抹除。尽管他的概念影响了涂尔干与布迪厄，他仍缺席于欧洲及美国社会学史，这种缺席清楚体现了上述抹除。此类缺席助长了一种持久印象：社会学主要是一门欧洲学科，未曾受到其他传统社会思想的影响。即使历史学家研究社会科学的殖民起源，欧洲人所遭遇、利用或挪用的思想传统也常常被噤声。因此，使伊本·赫勒敦去殖民化，意味着找回塑造欧洲思想的一份思想遗产，为多元的社会学史开辟道路。这不是为了贬低涂尔干、布迪厄，或任何与伊本·赫勒敦思想发生共鸣的社会学家、人类学家，而是为了说明：殖民主义如何创造一个思想在其中流通的全球领域，而殖民权力又如何使这一领域形成不均衡的结构。
